must_remember: The Stern-Gerlach experiment was conducted in 1922 by Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach using a beam of silver (Ag) atoms.
An inhomogeneous (non-uniform) magnetic field is strictly required to exert a net translational force on magnetic dipoles.
A uniform magnetic field only exerts a torque and causes precession, resulting in no translational deflection or beam splitting.
Silver atoms in the ground state have total orbital angular momentum $L = 0$, meaning the observed splitting into two components is due entirely to electron spin ($S = 1/2$).
The number of split components for a given angular momentum quantum number $j$ is given by $N = 2j + 1$.
The force on a magnetic dipole in an inhomogeneous field along the z-axis is $F_z = \mu_z \frac{d B_z}{d z}$.
Classical physics incorrectly predicts a continuous smearing or broad single band instead of discrete traces.
The Bohr magneton $\mu_B = \frac{e \hbar}{2 m_e}$ serves as the natural unit for expressing electron magnetic moments.

glossary.meaning: A magnetic field that varies in space, possessing a non-zero spatial derivative (gradient), necessary to exert a translational force on a magnetic dipole.
The quantum mechanical phenomenon where the direction of the angular momentum vector can only take specific quantized orientations relative to a reference axis.
A physical constant and natural unit for expressing the magnetic dipole moment of an electron caused by its orbital or spin angular momentum.
The atom used in the original Stern-Gerlach experiment, chosen because its single valence electron in an s-orbital ($L=0$) isolates the spin magnetic moment.
The ratio of the magnetic dipole moment to the angular momentum; for electron spin, $g_s \approx 2$.
A force that causes linear acceleration of a particle, generated in the Stern-Gerlach setup by the interaction between a magnetic dipole and a field gradient.

comparisons.title: Uniform vs. Inhomogeneous Magnetic Fields
rows: Constant magnitude and direction ($\frac{d B}{d z} = 0$)
Varies in space with a non-zero gradient ($\frac{d B}{d z} \neq 0$)
Non-zero net translational force ($F_z = \mu_z \frac{d B_z}{d z}$)
Exerts torque, causes precession without spatial splitting
Splits the atomic beam into discrete traces corresponding to $m_s$
